title: Unified Theory Of Wiggles
definition: A theory that proposes a continuous, scale-invariant framework from the Planck length to planetary ecosystems, with all phenomena being reformulated as interoperable wiggles within a single, dynamic continuum.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine everything in the universe as a series of gentle waves or movements. These waves interact in a complex way that creates all that we see and experience.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: The Unified Theory of Wiggles suggests that reality is defined by the act of wiggling, uniting quantum mechanics, biology, and geology within a single framework.
difficulty_levels.expert: The Unified Theory of Wiggles challenges the traditional distinction between object and process, providing a novel insight into the relationship between wiggles at the fundamental level and emergent phenomena.

extra_fields.insight: The Unified Theory of Wiggles unites various disciplines under a single framework, providing a deeper understanding of the interconnectedness of all phenomena in the universe.
